title: Magical Duels
audit_comment: CHAPTER 5 of the DMO (printed pp. 96-117), the dueling system closing in one round: the arena construction protocol with the consent doctrine, the balance-of-power cap, the corridor geometry (ten spaces plus the highest contributed levels, capped at thirty), the five-type doctrine with PR = level + nine, the Table 25 interactions grid, the Table 26 movement bands, the 1d20 spell combat with the lock rules, the character power scores and counter-spell doctrine, the item rules (the 6d6/8d6/9d6 leech caps, the protection power-score read at 14), the specialist gates, the friendly, death and service stakes ladders with the plane-blow and disintegration chances, the mediator duties, the special dueling characteristics (the five groups and the quantified individual abilities), and the Calvin-and-Delsenora worked duel.
audit_anchor: // ---- R227: the wis mental save wiring audit ----
prev_record: in one round - TEN boxes flip

banner.title: MAGICAL DUELS - DMO Chapter 5 closes: the arena protocol (the one-turn circling chant, the restart on disturbance, the mediator's protective spell, the contributed memorized spells lost as cast, the secret recording, the compulsion and threat consent doctrine), the balance-of-power cap at the weaker level, the corridor geometry (a 12-to-30-space corridor, ten base spaces plus each side's highest contribution, thirty at most between, thirty-two at largest), the four-step round with the advantage doctrine (the highest single spell, the 1d10 tie, the shift on destruction), the five-type doctrine with PR = level + nine, the Table 25 interactions grid and Table 26 movement bands, the 1d20-vs-PR combat with the lock rules and the Rary-Serten reads, the character power scores of Table 27 with the counter-spell doctrine and the 1d6-or-1d4-push personal combat, the item rules (the scroll of protection at PR 15 MV 1, the 6d6, 8d6 and 9d6 item leech caps, the 14 protection read, the absolute arena blockers), the specialist gates with the opposition-school +1, the friendly, death and service stakes ladders (the death bands running 2d6 to 10d6 damage with the 20 and 40 percent plane blows and the 50 percent disintegration), the mediator duties, the special dueling characteristics (the mental, summoning, illusion, reversible and teleportation groups, the demishadow and shadow magic reads, the earthquake counters, the wish reads), and the Calvin-and-Delsenora worked duel at ten spaces.
banner.provenance: verified against printed pp. 96-117 of the uploaded DMO session capture (part 2, printed page N at OCR page N+90); the arena protocol from pp. 96-97, the corridor and combat rules from pp. 97-101, Tables 25 and 26 from p. 99, Table 27 from p. 101, the character rules from pp. 103-104, the item and specialist rules from pp. 104-105, the stakes ladders from pp. 105-107, the special characteristics from pp. 108-116, the worked duel from pp. 116-117. The death ladder prints an 18-22 band after the 13-18 band, overlapping at 18; both bands are pinned verbatim in row order with the note here.
banner.sentinel: the gap census after this round: 69 closed, 27 open - Chapter 5 is DONE in one round, seventeen boxes flip (sixteen children and the parent); the DMO arc continues with Chapter 6 (True Dweomers, pp. 118-141).

bools.name: detArenaRestartOnDisturbance
bools.comment: the restart rule: if the combatants' concentration is disturbed before the arena is complete, the preparations begin again (printed p. 96).

bools.comment: the no-self rule: combatants are constructs in the arena - no casting on oneself; a cure heals nothing, a teleport goes nowhere (printed p. 98).

bools.name: detSpellsAffectConstructs
bools.comment: the construct doctrine: spells restrict the opponent's actions until thrown off, never controlling or imprisoning him directly (printed p. 98).

bools.name: detDetectIdentifies
bools.comment: the identification: spells are not readily identifiable; detect magic and the spellcraft proficiency can identify them (printed p. 98).

bools.name: detDefensiveMayStay
bools.comment: the defensive exception: a defensive spell may remain in the caster's space instead of crossing (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detMustMoveOneSpace
bools.comment: the movement floor: most spells must move at least one space every round unless locked in combat (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detCastingSimultaneous
bools.comment: the dueling cast: all spellcasting during a duel is simultaneous (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detCastingNotDisrupted
bools.comment: the dueling cast: spells cannot be disrupted as in a normal encounter (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detArenaSuppliesComponents
bools.comment: the component supply: no additional components required - pyrotechnics works in an arena with no fire source (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detSpellAppearsAhead
bools.comment: the cast placement: a spell appears in the space immediately ahead of the caster, or in the caster's space if defensive (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detNoMoveOnCastRound
bools.comment: the cast placement: no spell moves on the round it is cast (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detAttackMustFightDefense
bools.comment: the attack doctrine: an attack spell must conduct combat with any opposing defensive spell it meets, may fight leeches at the advantaged caster's choice, ignores missiles and attacks (printed p. 99).

bools.name: detDefenseMustFightAttack
bools.comment: the defense doctrine: a defensive spell must fight opposing attacks, may fight leeches, generally ignores missiles, always ignores other defenses, and vanishes at the opponent's square (printed p. 99).

bools.name: detLeechMustFightLeech
bools.comment: the leech doctrine: a leech must fight opposing leeches, may fight attacks or defenses, ignores missiles (printed p. 99).

bools.name: detLeechSaveHalf
bools.comment: the leech strike: saving throw vs. spell reduces the damage by half (printed p. 99).

bools.name: detADMustFightAD
bools.comment: the attack/defense doctrine: an AD spell must fight opposing defensive and attack spells, may fight leeches or missiles at the advantaged caster's choice (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detADSaveOrCombat
bools.comment: the AD strike: the opponent saves vs. spell or makes a spell combat roll to avoid the damage (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detMissileIgnoresMost
bools.comment: the missile doctrine: a missile may fight attack/defense spells, ignores missiles, leeches, attacks and most defenses (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detMoveOrderClosestFirst
bools.comment: the movement order: the spell closest to the opponent always moves first, then the next, and so on (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detFriendlyStackingOk
bools.comment: the friendly stack: one character's spells freely move through each other or share a space; the fastest moves first when stacked (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detNoBackwardMove
bools.comment: the one-way rule: spells never move backward unless forced by an opposing spell's special ability (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detFailIfHigher
bools.comment: the combat read: a roll higher than the power rank fails, equal or less succeeds (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detLockOnBothFail
bools.comment: the lock: both spells failing locks them in place (printed p. 101).

bools.name: detLockOnEqualPRTie
bools.comment: the lock: two spells with the same power scores tying each other also locks (printed p. 101).

bools.name: detHigherRollWins
bools.comment: the double success: with both succeeding, the higher roll destroys the lower (printed p. 101).

bools.name: detWinningSpellFinishesMove
bools.comment: the victory move: a winning spell that was moving may finish its move after the battle (printed p. 101).

bools.name: detOneCombatPerPairPerRound
bools.comment: the combat cap: one spell may fight several battles a round, but any one pair only once (printed p. 101).

bools.name: detLockedBlockPassage
bools.comment: the lock: locked spells block all passage, even spells that could normally ignore the opposing spell (printed p. 101).

bools.name: detHighestMVCheckedFirst
bools.comment: the multi-spell check: with multiple opposing spells and no lock, the highest movement rate is checked first (printed p. 101).

bools.name: detDisadvantagedAnnouncesType
bools.comment: the type announcement: the disadvantaged caster must announce his spell's type; the advantaged caster need not (printed p. 100).

bools.name: detCharMoveBackward
bools.comment: the duelist move: unlike spells, characters move forward or backward (printed p. 103).

bools.name: detSavingThrowsByCasterLevel
bools.comment: the duel save: the saving-throws-by-caster-level optional rule is always used in duels (printed p. 103).

bools.name: detAbilityBonusesNeverApply
bools.comment: the duel save: bonuses for high ability scores never apply during a duel (printed p. 103).

bools.name: detZeroHpLoses
bools.comment: the knockout: characters reduced to zero hit points or less lose the duel (printed p. 103).

bools.name: detLingeringBlocksButCounters
bools.comment: the lingering read: a hindered character cannot move or cast into the arena but may cast counter spells (printed p. 103).

bools.name: detPositiveHpNeverRemoved
bools.comment: the endurance rule: a character with positive hit points can never be removed from the arena or forced to end the duel by duel magic (printed p. 103).

bools.name: detCharLockDestroysAttacker
bools.comment: the character lock: when a character combats a spell, a lock destroys the attacking spell instead (printed p. 103).

bools.name: detCounterBothDestroyed
bools.comment: the counter spell: if the counter wins or locks, both the attacking and counter spells are destroyed; if the counter loses, the attack lands (printed p. 103).

bools.name: detUnlimitedCountersPerRound
bools.comment: the counter flow: any number of counter spells per round if memorized; countering does not prevent a later cast (printed p. 103).

bools.name: detDefenseVanishesAtOpponent
bools.comment: the defense read: defense spells vanish at the opponent's space; one may be cast in the character's own space as a stationary guard (printed p. 103).

bools.name: detPushIntoSpellTriggers
bools.comment: the push read: forced movement into a space with an opposing spell makes the spell take effect (printed p. 104).

bools.name: detNoCastWhileEngaged
bools.comment: the engagement bar: no spellcasting while engaged in character combat, and counter spells cannot be used against a character (printed p. 104).

bools.name: detPowerCheckIdentify
bools.comment: the spellcraft read: a character may identify an opposing spell with a power check instead of moving or casting (printed p. 104).

bools.name: detSpellRevealedAtSquare
bools.comment: the reveal: opposing spells are revealed when they enter a character's square (printed p. 103).

bools.name: detNoEquipmentInArena
bools.comment: the mind-only rule: no equipment can be carried into the arena; the opponents enter only in their minds (printed p. 104).

bools.name: detStoringItemsWork
bools.comment: the storing items: rings of spell storing, magical scrolls and rods of absorption can create spells in a duel (printed p. 104).

bools.name: detWandsUsuallyBanned
bools.comment: the item bar: wands, staves, potions and miscellaneous items and most rods usually cannot be used unless both agree (printed p. 104).

bools.name: detDeviceLevelSaves
bools.comment: the item save: an effect from a device uses the device level for the saving throw, not the wielder's (printed p. 104).

bools.name: detProtectiveBonusesVsSpellsOnly
bools.comment: the protection read: protective bonuses raise the power score against spells, not for personal combat (printed p. 104).

bools.name: detAcNoEffect
bools.comment: the AC bar: armor class has no effect on a duel; bracers of defense do not help (printed p. 104).

bools.name: detAttackBonusPersonalOnly
bools.comment: the weapon read: attack bonuses from magical weapons raise the power score for personal combat only (printed p. 104).

bools.name: detArenaBlockersAbsolute
bools.comment: the arena blockers: antimagic shell, prismatic sphere, the Otiluke spheres, wall spells and protection-from-magic scrolls can never be incorporated, even by agreement (printed p. 105).

bools.name: detSpecialistSavesApply
bools.comment: the specialist read: saving-throw adjustments from the school of specialization apply during duels unless forgone, at an extra turn of preparation (printed p. 105).

bools.name: detWildSurgesNever
bools.comment: the wild read: wild surges never occur in the stable arena environment (printed p. 105).

bools.name: detLevelVariationBothWildMages
bools.comment: the wild read: level variations possible only if both combatants are wild mages (printed p. 105).

bools.name: detElementalistBoostBothElementalists
bools.comment: the elementalist read: the higher-than-normal cast applies only if both combatants are elementalists (printed p. 105).

bools.name: detEndOnNoSpellsOrHp
bools.comment: the end conditions: a duel always ends when a combatant runs out of spells or hit points; the combatants choose one or both (printed p. 105).

bools.name: detAutoEndWhenMet
bools.comment: the binding: once set, the duel automatically ends when the condition is met, even if minds change (printed p. 105).

bools.name: detSurrenderAlwaysAllowed
bools.comment: the exit: a character can always end a duel early by surrendering and accepting defeat (printed p. 105).

bools.name: detSpellLossAsCast
bools.comment: the spell loss: spells lost after a duel are gone as though cast, their components consumed (printed p. 106).

bools.name: detContributedAlwaysLost
bools.comment: the spell loss: spells contributed to the arena are always lost (printed p. 106).

bools.name: detWinnerCapAtCast
bools.comment: the spell loss: the winner cannot lose more spell levels than were cast, but the loser can (printed p. 106).

bools.name: detExcessPermanentIfDeath
bools.comment: the overdraw: permanent if fought to the death, else one point restored per full day of rest (printed p. 106).

bools.name: detMassiveDamageNA
bools.comment: the damage note: the Death From Massive Damage rule does not apply in duels (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detCharmIgnoresResistances
bools.comment: the service charm: unaffected by magic resistance, racial charm resistance or high ability scores - the winner bores into the psyche (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detUnconsciousKillable
bools.comment: the unconscious risk: anyone with a weapon can kill an unconscious character with a single blow (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detBlownEquipmentStays
bools.comment: the plane blow: the loser leaves a pile of dust; destroyed equipment remains behind and a wish recovers him (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detDisintegrateNoRegeneration
bools.comment: the death read: regeneration is ineffective; only a wish restores a disintegrated character (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detBand4EquipmentSaveFire
bools.comment: the death ladder: failed breath save - equipment saves vs. magical fire on the 18-22 band (printed p. 106).

bools.name: detBand5EquipmentSaveLightning
bools.comment: the death ladder: equipment saves vs. lightning on the 23-plus band (printed p. 106).

bools.name: detServiceGeasLiftNeeds
bools.comment: the service read: the 19-plus geas lifts only by a wish, dispel magic or remove curse from a higher-level caster (printed p. 106).

bools.name: detWinnerTempCappedAtDuel
bools.comment: the damage cap: a victor cannot suffer more temporary damage than was suffered in the duel; the loser can suffer more normal damage (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detInterferenceEndsDuel
bools.comment: the interference rule: any attack on a duelist, successful or not, disrupts the arena and ends the duel (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detBothVictorsOnInterference
bools.comment: the interference rule: both characters count as victor for the aftereffects, other terms rendered invalid (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detTouchCombatantsEnds
bools.comment: the interference rule: touching the combatants, handing them equipment or casting spells on them ends the duel; shouting advice is allowed if the protective spell permits (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detMediatorAttacksNoEffect
bools.comment: the interference rule: attacks on the mediator or the protective spell have no effect on the duel (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detMediatorChoosesIsolation
bools.comment: the mediator's role: he decides how isolated the combatants are (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detMediatorSearchesContraband
bools.comment: the mediator's role: it is traditional to search each combatant for contraband, physically, to foil nondetection (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detMediatorTouchEnds
bools.comment: the mediator's role: the mediator can end the construction or the duel just by touching a combatant (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detMediatorNoCompulsion
bools.comment: the mediator's role: under no special compulsion toward fairness unless duelists take precautions such as a geas (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detMediatorMayIncludeSelf
bools.comment: the mediator's role: a large protective spell can include the mediator; prismatic sphere allows free passage in and out (printed p. 107).

bools.name: detMentalTemporaryOnly
bools.comment: the mental-attack group: charm, command, confusion and their kin have only a temporary effect - the victim cannot move or cast but may counter (printed p. 108).

bools.name: detNeverCompelledToLeave
bools.comment: the mental-attack group: duelists can never be compelled to leave the arena or perform unwanted actions (printed p. 108).

bools.name: detSummoningCounterOnly
bools.comment: the summoning group: while a creature summoning occupies his space the opponent can cast only counter spells and must fight with his power score (printed p. 108).

bools.name: detSummoningLockPersists
bools.comment: the summoning group: a lock does not destroy a summoning spell - it attacks again next round, unlike normal character-vs-spell combat (printed p. 108).

bools.name: detIllusionAnyType
bools.comment: the illusion group: phantasmal-force spells can duplicate any type, chosen at casting and never changed (printed p. 108).

bools.name: detIllusionTypeFixedAtCast
bools.comment: the illusion group: the type is chosen when cast and cannot change (printed p. 108).

bools.name: detIllusionDefenseLockDestroys
bools.comment: the illusion group: employed as a defense, any lock destroys the illusion unless the opponent summons a creature (printed p. 108).

bools.name: detReversedOpposite
bools.comment: the reversible group: reversed forms usually function opposite - a reversed defense is an attack; a reversed leech is still a leech (printed p. 108).

bools.name: detReverseCountersReverse
bools.comment: the reversible group: a spell's reverse always counters itself and vice versa (printed p. 108).

bools.name: detTeleportIgnoresBarrierLocks
bools.comment: the teleportation group: instantaneous-travel spells cannot be locked by physical barriers - a lock means the spells ignore each other (printed p. 108).

bools.name: detTeleportCounterLockDestroys
bools.comment: the teleportation group: used as a counter spell, a lock still destroys both spells (printed p. 108).

bools.name: detWishNoAgingUnlessLost
bools.comment: the wish and limited wish read: no aging unless actually lost from memory in the aftermath (printed pp. 113 and 116).

bools.name: detHasteSlowMutual
bools.comment: the haste read: haste automatically destroys and is automatically destroyed by slow (printed p. 112).

bools.name: detShieldDefeatsMagicMissile
bools.comment: the shield read: missiles must battle it, and it always defeats magic missile (printed p. 115).

bools.name: detTransmuteDefeatsWallOfStone
bools.comment: the transmute rock to mud read: it always defeats wall of stone (printed p. 116).

bools.name: detFlyLevitateCounterTransmute
bools.comment: the fly and levitate read: both always counter transmute rock to mud (printed p. 112).

bools.name: detTrueSeeingDefeatsIllusions
bools.comment: the true seeing read: it always defeats illusions (printed p. 116).

bools.name: detStabilizeIneffective
bools.comment: the ineffective trio: stabilize, windwild and wildzone do nothing in a dueling arena (printed pp. 115-116).

bools.name: detMindBlankCountersLeeches
bools.comment: the mind blank read: cannot be locked by mind attacks; it counters all leech spells and mental attacks (printed p. 113).

bools.name: detPermanencyNoConLoss
bools.comment: the permanency read: used in a duel it does not drain Constitution, even if lost from memory afterward (printed p. 113).

bools.name: detNeutralizePoisonCounters
bools.comment: the neutralize poison read: it automatically counters poisonous spells such as stinking cloud and cloudkill (printed p. 113).

bools.name: detRemoveParalysisCounters
bools.comment: the remove paralysis read: it automatically counters all hold spells and paralysis (printed p. 114).

bools.name: detRaiseDeadCountersDamage
bools.comment: the raise dead and reincarnate read: they counter any spell that inflicts damage (printed p. 114).

bools.name: detCrystalbrittleDefeatsMetal
bools.comment: the crystalbrittle read: it automatically defeats wall of iron and any other metal-mass spell, in combat and as a counter (printed p. 110).

bools.name: detDisintegrateDefeatsBarriers
bools.comment: the disintegrate read: it always defeats solid-barrier spells such as wall spells (printed p. 110).

bools.name: detDispelDestroysOnLoss
bools.comment: the dispel magic read: if locked or defeated it can still destroy the opposing spell with a normal dispel roll; it dissipates at the opponent's space (printed pp. 110-111).

bools.name: detExWithdrawForcesCombat
bools.comment: the worked duel: withdraw's special ability forces leeches and missiles to fight it despite the advantage (printed p. 117).

bools.name: detExArenaTenSpaces
bools.comment: the worked duel: no contributions, so ten spaces between the combatants (printed p. 116).

chains.name: detServiceLadder
chains.comment: the service stakes ladder (printed p. 106): by contributed spell levels the loser is charmed at 0-6, plus a suggestion at 7-12, plus a geas at 13-18, and falls under domination at 19-plus; the codes run charm, suggestion, geas, domination.

tables.name: detT25Grid
tables.comment: the Table 25 spell interactions grid (printed p. 99): rows the acting spell type A, D, AD, L, M; columns the opposing type met; codes - 0 pass, 1 combat, 2 the advantaged caster decides, 3 generally ignore.
col_comments: meeting an attack spell: attacks pass attacks, defenses and attacks fight, AD fights, leeches let the advantage decide, missiles pass (printed p. 99).
meeting a defense spell: attacks must fight, defenses pass each other, AD fights, leeches let the advantage decide, missiles generally ignore (printed p. 99).
meeting an attack/defense spell: attacks, defenses and attacks/defenses fight; leeches and missiles let the advantage decide (printed p. 99).
meeting a leech spell: attacks and defenses let the advantage decide, attack/defenses let the advantage decide, leeches fight leeches, missiles pass (printed p. 99).
meeting a missile spell: attacks pass, defenses generally ignore, attack/defenses let the advantage decide, leeches pass, missiles pass (printed p. 99).

tables.name: detT26Grid
tables.comment: the Table 26 spell movement grid (printed p. 99): five range bands, touch through 101-plus yards, each with its arena movement rate; level-varied ranges move with the range.
col_comments: the movement rate by range band: touch or zero moves one, 1-20 yards two, 21-50 three, 51-100 four, 101-plus and instantaneous-huge effects five (printed p. 99).

tables.name: detT27Grid
tables.comment: the Table 27 character power scores (printed p. 101): five ability bands, 14-or-less through 18-plus, with the bonus and the power score; wizards and bards use Intelligence, priests, paladins and rangers Wisdom.
col_comments: the ability bonus: zero at 14 or less, one at 15, two at 16, three at 17, four at 18 or more (printed p. 101).
the power score: nine at 14 or less, ten at 15, eleven at 16, twelve at 17, thirteen at 18 or more (printed p. 101).

tables.name: detFriendlyStakes
tables.comment: the friendly-competition stakes ladder (printed p. 105): four bands by contributed spell levels, the loser's temporary damage dice and forfeited spell levels, the winner's lost spell levels; a dash marks a band where nothing is lost, and the loser's hit points always return to normal.
col_comments: the loser's temporary damage dice: nothing at 0-6, 2d6 at 7-12, 4d6 at 13-18, 8d6 at 19-plus (printed p. 105).
the loser's temporary damage die size: d6 throughout (printed p. 105).
the loser's forfeited spell-level dice: nothing, 2d4, 4d4, 8d4 (printed p. 105).
the loser's forfeited spell-level die size: d4 throughout (printed p. 105).
the winner's lost spell-level dice: nothing until 13-18 where 1d6, 4d6 at 19-plus (printed p. 105).
the winner's lost spell-level die size: d6 where lost (printed p. 105).

tables.name: detDeathStakes
tables.comment: the death-duel stakes ladder (printed pp. 105-106): five bands by contributed spell levels; the loser always saves vs. death or dies on the first three bands, the last two use the breath-weapon save with the explosion; the winner's temporary damage and lost spell levels ride beside the loser's.
col_comments: the loser's damage dice: 2d6, 4d6, 6d6, 8d6, 10d6 across the five bands (printed pp. 105-106).
the loser's damage die size: d6 throughout (printed pp. 105-106).
the loser's lost spell-level dice: none on the first band, then 4d4, 8d4, 12d4, 18d4 (printed pp. 105-106).
the loser's lost spell-level die size: d4 throughout (printed pp. 105-106).
the winner's lost spell-level dice: none, 1d6, 2d6, 4d6, 2d6 (printed pp. 105-106).
the winner's lost spell-level die size: d6 throughout (printed pp. 105-106).
the winner's temporary damage dice: none on the first two bands, 1d6, 2d6, 4d6 (printed pp. 105-106).
the winner's temporary damage die size: d6 throughout (printed pp. 105-106).

the worked-duel clairvoyance: level 3 plus nine is PR 12 (printed p. 116)
the worked-duel withdraw: level 2 plus nine is PR 11 (printed p. 116)
the worked-duel monster summoning II: level 4 plus nine is PR 13 (printed p. 117)
the worked-duel magic missile: level 1 plus nine is PR 10 (printed p. 117)
the worked-duel dispel magic and animate object: PRs 12 and 15 (printed p. 117)
the arena distance: ten spaces plus five plus three is 18 (printed p. 97)
the corridor cap: the largest arena is 30 between plus two duelists (printed p. 97)
the character power score: base nine plus the Table 27 top bonus is 13 (printed p. 101)
the Table 27 read: a 15 ability gives bonus 1 and power score 10 (printed p. 101)
the Table 26 read: touch moves one, 101-plus moves five (printed p. 99)
the Table 25 read: an attack meets a defense - combat; a defense meets a missile - generally ignore (printed p. 99)
the Table 25 read: leeches fight leeches; missiles pass attacks (printed p. 99)
the Table 25 read: attack/defense fights attacks, defenses and its own kind (printed p. 99)
the friendly ladder: the 7-12 band costs the loser 2d6 and 2d4 (printed p. 105)
the friendly ladder: the 19-plus band costs the loser 8d6 and 8d4, the winner 4d6 (printed p. 105)
the death ladder: the first band is 2d6 damage with the death save (printed p. 105)
the death ladder: the 23-plus band costs the loser 10d6 and 18d4, the winner 4d6 temporary (printed p. 106)
the service ladder: 0-6 charm, 7-12 plus suggestion, 13-18 plus geas, 19-plus domination (printed p. 106)

table_checks.note: the protection read: 11 plus 2 plus 1 is 14 (printed p. 104)
the specialist read: dispel magic at 12 gains one against illusionists for 13 (printed p. 105)
the Johan read: unseen servant at 10 minus the 5 variation is 5 (printed p. 105)
the freeze read: 10d4 at +2 per die is the 20-damage cap (printed p. 113)
the chant and fire purge reads: two rounds and ten rounds with nine disruptible (printed pp. 109 and 111)
the enervation read: a 12th-level caster drains three levels (printed p. 111)
the lock read: the Rary-Serten pair at PR 10 each ties on equal rolls (printed p. 101)
the worked duel: Calvin's 20 against a PR-12 clairvoyance fails; Delsenora's 9 against 11 succeeds (printed p. 117)
the balance example: the cap is the wizard's level, seven (printed p. 97)
the plane blows: 20 percent on the 18-22 band, 40 percent on the 23-plus band (printed p. 106)
the disintegration read: half the deaths leave dust (printed p. 107)
